title: Control mapping and acceptance criteria for RBAC v2, SIEM exports, and evidence automation
content:
Purpose:
This doc synthesizes SOC 2 / ISO 27001 control mappings with the RBAC v2 rollout, the audit-log schema changes, SIEM export requirements, and the current state of evidence automation. Its goal is to provide:
- A concise control mapping and acceptance criteria list auditors will expect
- A gap analysis summary with remediation priorities
- An "auditor Q&A" cheat-sheet linking assertions to concrete artifacts and automation outputs

Scope:
Applies to the RBAC v2 feature set (authorization model, assignment workflows, service-account model), the standardized audit-log schema produced by the gateway and runtime, and the SIEM export pipeline that forwards logs to Splunk/Datadog/Elastic. Private deployment telemetry (on-prem) is covered where the private control plane produces equivalent artifacts.

Executive summary (short):
- We have a completed RBAC v2 spec and an initial implementation in dedicated-hosted and private control planes.
- Audit-log schema v2 (JSON-lines) is implemented for all auth/permission decisions, and SIEM export supports both CEF and NDJSON formats.
- Evidence automation covers log collection and snapshot bundles for hosted customers; gaps remain in per-tenant evidence collection for Private deployments and long-term log retention proof for ISO requirements.

Control mapping approach:
- For each SOC 2 criterion (CC1x/CC2x mapping), identify the ISO 27001 control(s) most relevant, then enumerate the concrete artifact(s) we will provide. Acceptance criteria emphasize machine-verifiable artifacts (log files, signed manifests, automation job outputs, configuration versions).
- Where possible, assertions should reference automation outputs (e.g., terraform plan hash, role-binding export, audit-log manifests) rather than only screenshots.

Representative control mappings (high-level):
- SOC 2:Logical access controls (CC6) -> ISO 27001: A.9 (Access control)
  - Artifacts: RBAC v2 role catalog export (CSV/JSON), role-permission matrix, recent access reviews (attestation CSV), change PR history with approved reviewers (GitHub links).
  - Acceptance: Role catalog includes role id, description, granted permissions, last_modified, owner, and deploy-tag.

- SOC 2:System operations and availability -> ISO 27001: A.12 (Operations security)
  - Artifacts: Scheduled job run logs for evidence automation, SIEM forwarder health metrics, alerts/responses for failed exports.
  - Acceptance: Automation job success rate > 98% over last 30d and documented manual fallback procedure.

- SOC 2:Change management -> ISO 27001: A.14 (System acquisition, development and maintenance)
  - Artifacts: Change ticket ID, deployment plan, rollbacks, canary logs for RBAC v2 rollout.
  - Acceptance: All RBAC config changes show an associated ticket and CI pipeline run id.

RBAC v2 acceptance criteria (concrete):
- Role model: Roles are defined with stable IDs, human-friendly names, and canonical permission sets. Accept if role export includes fields: role_id, name, description, permissions[], owner_email, last_updated_iso, version_tag.
- Assignment evidence: Every binding (user/serviceaccount -> role) has an audit event when created/removed. Accept if binding operations are present in audit-log stream for the period requested.
- Separation of duties/critical privilege review: Critical roles (defined list) must have at least quarterly attestations; acceptance requires attestation artifacts (csv + signer) within last 90 days.
- Override/temporary elevation workflow: Elevation requests are timeboxed, logged, and require approver signature. Evidence: elevation request audit events + approval chain.

Audit log schema (v2) — minimal fields required for auditor acceptance:
- timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
- event_id (UUID v4)
- service (gateway | runtime | control-plane)
- event_type (authn | authz | role_change | elevation | system_change | export)
- principal_type (user | service_account | system)
- principal_id
- resource_type (role | binding | model | deployment | secret | api_key)
- resource_id
- action (create | update | delete | allow | deny | request | approve | revoke)
- decision (allowed | denied | error)
- decision_reasons (array encoded as JSON-string)
- request_context (ip, user_agent, request_id) encoded as JSON-string
- correlation_id
- raw_payload_hash (sha256)
- signature (optional)

Notes on schema and evidentiary value:
- Auditors prefer JSON-lines exports filtered for a window (e.g., last 90 days) plus a signed manifest of hashes to prove integrity.
- We produce a manifest file with per-file sha256 + a signed bundle certificate created by the automation runner.

SIEM export formats & configuration expectations:
- Supported output formats: NDJSON (preferred), CEF for legacy SIEMs, and syslog (TLS).
- Forwarding guarantees: at-least-once delivery with sequence numbers in the envelope to aid deduplication.
- Health metrics: forwarder uptime, backlog length, last_acknowledged_offset.
- Acceptance: Exported artifacts include export-log-YYYYMMDD.ndjson.gz and export-manifest-YYYYMMDD.sig.

Evidence automation status (as of last_modified):
- Hosted: full automation implemented. Jobs: daily-log-bundle, weekly-attestation, monthly-retention-audit. Bundles include logs + manifest + index.
- Dedicated/Private: partial automation. We have the automation runner packaged but tenant-side scheduling is manual for on-prem customers. Evidence bundles can be produced on request with engineering assistance.
- Gaps: retention proof automation for Private instances (ISO requires proof of retention schedule across 2+ years for some controls) and cross-tenant integrity proofs in older log shards.

Gap analysis (summary):
- High (P0) gaps:
  1) Private deployment retention automation not available — impacts ISO27001 A.12.3 and SOC 2 evidence for long-term logs.
  2) Per-tenant signed manifest for legacy archives older than 6 months — integrity proof missing.
- Medium (P1):
  1) Some audit events (rare) do not include request_context.ip for internal system actors — reduces traceability.
  2) SIEM export health dashboard lacks per-tenant backlog alerting.
- Low (P2):
  1) Minor schema fields optional for backward compatibility (e.g., decision_reasons occasionally null).

Remediation plan (next actions):
- P0 Owner: Eng-servicing + Security. Deliver within 8 weeks: private-retention-runner (agent) + automated manifest signing and remote submission to customer-provided S3/KMS.
- P1 Owner: Observability. Deliver within 4 weeks: add ip for internal system principals and SIEM backlog alerting dashboard.
- P2 Owner: Applied-ML/Platform. Deliver within 6 weeks: strong schema validation in pipeline and scheduled backfill for missing decision_reasons where possible.

Auditor Q&A prep (likely questions and evidence pointers):
Q: How do you demonstrate that role changes are controlled and reviewed?
A: Provide: role-catalog-export.json (full history), role-change audit events filtered by ticket id (JIRA-SEC-XXX), reviewer approvals in GitHub PRs, and attestation CSV for critical roles.

Q: Can you show a full chain of custody for a binding creation?
A: Provide audit-log slice with event_id for the binding.create, the corresponding IAM ticket id in the event, the CI pipeline run id that deployed the change (if applicable), and the manifest signature that covers the file.

Q: How do you prove logs haven’t been tampered with?
A: Provide signed manifest files (sha256) for the requested window, the automation runner signature (GPG/PKCS7), and forwarder health logs showing no backlog gaps. For hosted logs we also show storage immutability settings and versioned object metadata in S3.

Q: For Private deployments, what is the onus for evidence?
A: We provide the automation runner and documented runbook. Where requested we will perform a jointly-witnessed evidence extraction (eng run + customer approval). Acceptance criteria: extracted bundle + signed manifest + deployment config.

Q: Are SIEM exports reliable and complete?
A: Provide: export manifest with sequence numbers, forwarder ack logs, and a sample ndjson export for the window. Also show the forwarder health dashboard and any incident tickets for missed exports plus remediation steps.

Quick checklist for audit packet (minimum deliverables):
- RBAC role-catalog export (current + 90d history)
- Binding create/update/delete events (requested window) in ndjson + manifest.sig
- Signed manifest file for each exported ndjson file
- Evidence automation job run logs + job config yml
- Change tickets/PRs for RBAC schema changes and approvals
- Forwarder health metrics and backlog alerts screenshots (or API export)
- Attestation CSV for critical roles (most recent)

  "raw_payload_hash": "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924..."

Next steps and owners:
- Security: finalize the acceptance criteria matrix and add to compliance runbook (due 2025-02-28).
- Engineering (observability): implement per-tenant backlog alerting (due 2025-03-14).
- Platform/Infra: release private-runner v0.9 with manifest signing (due 2025-04-09).

Notes to reviewers:
- This document focuses on what auditors will want as machine-verifiable evidence. For review, please flag anything that requires cross-team escalation or has deployment cost implications.

End of document.
